headline: GOLD PLUNGES $160 ON US-IRAN STRIKES + WARSH SPEECH — Rate-Hike Bets Jump To 62% In One Week
snippet: Gold December futures opened August 31 at $4,483 per ounce — down from Friday's $4,598.89 close — as two forces compounded over the weekend: U.S. strikes on Iranian rocket launchers near the Strait of Hormuz (the first military escalation in a month) and Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole address warning the Fed still has 'work to do' on inflation. Brent crude surged above $90 per barrel on the strike news, importing fresh oil-driven inflation risk at the worst moment for rate bulls; COMEX probability of a 25bp rate hike at the September 15-16 FOMC jumped to 62% from roughly 40% a week prior. Gold's intraday low of $4,435 per ounce represents a $163 decline from Friday's high, and the dual macro shock arrives with the most data-intensive week of the year ahead — JOLTS, ADP, ISM, and the August NFP on September 4.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD DOUBLES SPYGLASS ZONE TO 330m DEPTH — 78.40 g/t Au Core Confirmed At Ontario Gold Rock Project
snippet: Dryden Gold Corp. (TSX-V: DRY) announced August 31 that drill hole DGR-073 at the Spyglass zone, Gold Rock Project in northwestern Ontario, returned 4.60 metres at 9.40 g/t gold including a 0.38-metre core at 78.40 g/t gold at a true vertical depth of 330 metres — approximately 140 metres below the zone's previously known base. All four holes in the current programme intersected visible gold in the predicted locations, confirming down-plunge continuity of the geological model. The expanded drilling approximately doubled the Spyglass footprint, adding roughly 110 metres by 50 metres of new mineralized area, while DGR-073 also independently intersected the Buccaneer zone at 370 metres depth. For retail investors: doubling a high-grade zone's vertical extent with visible gold confirmed in every hole is a grade-and-continuity combination that substantially de-risks the target ahead of resource estimation — a meaningful signal at current gold prices above $4,400.

headline: DOW -294, S&P -32, RATE-HIKE BETS AT 62% — US-Iran Escalation And Warsh Reshape September FOMC Calculus
snippet: U.S. equity markets fell broadly on August 31 — Dow -294 points (-0.6%), S&P 500 -32 points (-0.4%), Nasdaq -102 points (-0.4%) — after U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday and Iran's Revolutionary Guards responded with strikes on U.S. military bases in Jordan and UAE. Brent crude surged above $90 per barrel on supply-disruption premium, reviving the oil-inflation pass-through the Fed has cited throughout 2026 as a rationale for staying restrictive. Rate futures repriced the September 15-16 FOMC to 62% probability of a 25-basis-point hike, up from approximately 40% a week prior. Canada's TSX posted its second consecutive weekly decline led by metal mining shares. For retail investors in junior mining: August's record gold miner rally (+43% MSCI gold miners) now enters September with the macro context sharply shifted — the coming week's data prints will determine whether August's gains hold or give way to a Q3 consolidation.

headline: SILVER DEFIES GOLD SELLOFF, RISES 1% — Sixth Straight 46.3M oz Deficit And Industrial Demand Shield From Rate Shock
snippet: Silver spot rose $0.70 (+1.04%) to $67.10 per ounce on August 31 while gold fell more than 2% on US-Iran escalation and Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish speech — a divergence that reflects silver's dual monetary-and-industrial identity. Unlike gold, silver's demand base — solar panels, electronics, EV charging infrastructure, and since January 1, 2026, China's reclassification of silver as a strategic material — is largely insensitive to Fed rate policy. The structural backdrop reinforces the divergence: the World Silver Survey 2026 projects a sixth consecutive annual deficit at 46.3 million ounces, with total demand of 1,112.6 million ounces outpacing supply of 1,066.4 million ounces, and a cumulative 762 million troy ounces drawn from above-ground stocks since 2021. For retail investors: silver outperforming gold during a rate-shock event narrows the gold-silver ratio — historically, a declining gold-silver ratio during late-stage precious metals bull markets signals the beginning of speculative capital rotation into silver and silver miners.

headline: EXCELLON DEFINES 9,050 g/t Ag AND 14 g/t Au TARGETS AT TRES CERROS — Mallay Mine Adjacent, Drilling H1 2027
snippet: Excellon Resources Inc. (TSX-V: EXN) announced August 31 the definition of seven drill-ready target areas at its Tres Cerros exploration property in Peru, with surface grab samples returning up to 14 g/t gold and 9,050 g/t silver — grades consistent with high-sulphidation epithermal mineralisation. The 11,000-hectare property is prospective for both epithermal gold-silver and porphyry copper systems, and sits directly adjacent to the Mallay Mine, which resumed processing on July 2, 2026 and has since processed approximately 12,000 tonnes producing concentrates containing 29,200 ounces of silver. Environmental and archaeological baseline studies are complete; a DIA (environmental impact assessment) submission is targeted by end-2026, with initial drilling planned for H1 2027. For retail investors: grab samples are highly selective and are not representative of average grade, but 9,050 g/t Ag in surface samples on a project adjacent to a recently restarted silver mine — with infrastructure in place — represents a credible high-priority drill target less than a year from first drill results.

headline: NICOLA MINING: 753 g/t Ag AND 2.83 g/t Au IN RED EYE STOCKPILE — Merritt Mill Recovery Simulations Now Underway
snippet: Nicola Mining Inc. (TSX-V: NIM) announced August 31 that representative samples from two Red Eye Resources mill feed stockpiles (totalling approximately 1,500 tonnes) returned a weighted average grade of 2.83 g/t gold and 753.41 g/t silver, following the profit-share agreement announced on August 17. The samples — 47.82 kg drawn from a 1,200-tonne and a 300-tonne stockpile — will now advance to laboratory metallurgical simulations to maximize recovery before any decision is made to process the material at Nicola Mining's fully permitted Merritt Mill facility in British Columbia. For retail investors: Nicola Mining's toll-milling business model generates revenue from high-grade third-party material without the capital cost of mine development — at current prices ($4,450/oz Au and $67/oz Ag), the combined precious metals value of 1,500 tonnes at this grade is substantial if metallurgical recovery proves achievable.

headline: GRAPHANO ENERGY SECURES BLACK JACK DRILLING PERMITS — 19.8% Cg Average Grade From Quebec Graphite Discovery
snippet: Graphano Energy Ltd. (TSX-V: GEL) announced August 31 receipt of two Quebec exploration permits for its Black Jack graphite discovery: ATI-862 authorizes mechanical stripping over 1.1 hectares from September 15, 2026, and ATI-863 authorizes diamond drilling over 2.15 hectares from October 15, 2026. Spring 2026 grab samples from an exposed graphite-bearing horizon measuring approximately 110 metres by 15 metres returned 12.0% to 26.5% graphitic carbon (Cg), with an average of 19.8% Cg across 28 samples — 25 of 28 exceeding 15% Cg, the commercial grade threshold for battery anode feedstock. Black Jack sits approximately one kilometre northwest of the company's Black Pearl graphite showing in Quebec. For retail investors: natural flake graphite at 19.8% Cg average is high-grade for a discovery-stage project, and permit receipt means first drill results could arrive Q4 2026 — a potential catalyst in a graphite market where ex-China battery anode supply remains critically scarce.

headline: BLUE JAY GOLD DRILLS YUKON ANTIMONY AS CHINA BAN AND US DEFENSE DEADLINE INTENSIFY EX-CHINA RACE
snippet: Blue Jay Gold Corp. (TSX-V: JAY) announced August 31 the commencement of drilling at the Becker-Cochran antimony-silver occurrence within its Steller Gold Project in southern Yukon — one of the few active Western Hemisphere antimony exploration programmes. Antimony, used in flame retardants, semiconductors, and military munitions, was subject to Chinese export restrictions from September 2025, and EO 14415 (signed July 20, 2026) bars Chinese-origin critical minerals — including antimony — from U.S. defense procurement contracts as of January 1, 2027. Yukon-jurisdiction antimony occurrences are geologically rare in Canada's mineral-rich north; the hard 2027 deadline and China's near-monopoly on production (70%+ of global supply) mean any credible Western discovery is likely to attract significant strategic interest from both investors and defense-adjacent end-users in the coming months.

headline: CANADIAN GOLDFIELDS LAUNCHES MIMINISKA FALL PROGRAM — Soil Grids And Aeromagnetics Ahead Of Winter Drill At NW Ontario Gold
snippet: Canadian Goldfields Discovery Corp. (TSX-V: CGM) announced August 31 the commencement of its 2026 Fall Exploration Program at the Miminiska Gold Project in the Patricia Mining Division of northwestern Ontario. The programme includes an extensive soil geochemical survey, an airborne magnetic survey, and preparations for a winter camp supporting an anticipated winter drill programme — a systematic target-refinement approach before first drilling. The Miminiska area sits within the Patricia Gold Belt, associated with high-grade gold deposits in the Sioux Lookout region. For retail investors: this is a pre-drill programme announcement — the substance comes when results from the upcoming winter drill campaign return, likely in early 2027. The significance of this update is that it confirms a funded, methodical approach to target identification in one of Ontario's most historically productive gold belts.
